title: Investigation of the Anchoring Effect and its Occurrence Mechanism in LLM-driven Price Negotiation Simulation

live_model.evidence: Sec. 4.2 footnote list: "5 o1-2024-12-17"; o1 substituted as the buyer's reasoning model in the negotiation simulation (results table for buyer-LLM comparison).

prompt.location: Fig. 2-4 (templated system prompts with $PRODUCT/$TARGET_PRICE/$PERSONA placeholders), Table 1 (fully instantiated example)
prompt.note: gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (footnote 2) is also used as "GPT-4" seller/buyer with its own results row.

claim.metric: buyer achievement score, Anchoring condition (o1 as buyer vs. GPT-4o seller)
claim.location: Buyer-LLM achievement results table (o1 row), Sec. 5.1

data.source: CraigslistBargain dataset (He et al. 2018), 161 product listings

notes: 322 total simulated negotiations (161 items x Control/Anchoring/Informed) run across 6 LLM buyer/seller combinations for up to 20 turns each; the exact per-cell n for the o1-as-buyer condition is not restated and is only approximately derivable from the reported confidence intervals, so n_items=50 is an estimate. A low-temperature ChatGPT (undated) is also used as an auxiliary dialogue-act classifier (role A).
